record.original_question: Characterize the numerical semigroups S for which the omega-primality omega(S) is different from the type t(S).

evidence.quote: In [4] it is highlighted that numerical semigroups fulfilling omega(S) != t(S) are rare. A characterization for numerical semigroups fulfilling this condition should be welcomed.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A numerical semigroup is a subset S of the nonnegative integers N that is closed under addition, contains 0, and has finite complement in N. Let S be a numerical semigroup with minimal system of generators {n_1, ..., n_e}.

The type of S, denoted t(S), is the cardinality of the set PF(S) = {x ∈ Z \ S : x + s ∈ S for every s ∈ S \ {0}} of pseudo-Frobenius numbers of S.

For a nonzero element s ∈ S, the ω-primality of s in S, denoted ω_S(s), is the least positive integer N (or ∞ if no such N exists) such that whenever s divides a sum a_1 + a_2 + ... + a_n in S (i.e., (a_1 + ... + a_n) - s ∈ S) with each a_i ∈ S \ {0}, there exists a subset I ⊆ {1, ..., n} with |I| ≤ N such that s divides ∑_{i ∈ I} a_i in S. The ω-primality of S is defined by
   ω(S) = max{ ω_S(n_i) : i = 1, ..., e }.

It is known that ω(S) ≥ t(S) for every numerical semigroup S, and that equality ω(S) = t(S) holds for "most" numerical semigroups (in a computational sense), so that semigroups with ω(S) ≠ t(S) are comparatively rare.

Problem: Give an explicit characterization of the numerical semigroups S for which ω(S) ≠ t(S).
artifact.status_search_result: Web search returns work on computing ω-primality of numerical semigroups (algorithms, asymptotic ω-primality, mathematical programming approaches), but no source providing a complete characterization of numerical semigroups S satisfying ω(S) ≠ t(S). The status appears to remain open or at least unresolved in the literature surveyed, but no definitive resolution was located.

status_evidence.title: Computation of the ω-primality and asymptotic ω-primality with applications to numerical semigroups
status_evidence.snippet: Algorithms and formulas for computing ω-primality of numerical semigroups; does not give a characterization of when ω(S) ≠ t(S).
status_evidence.claim: Computational work on ω-primality, no characterization of ω(S) ≠ t(S).

status_evidence.title: An improved algorithm to compute the ω-primality
status_evidence.snippet: Improved algorithms for computing ω-primality but no closed-form characterization of when ω(S) differs from t(S).
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent computational papers do not resolve the characterization.

status_evidence.title: Asymptotic ω-Primality of Finitely Generated Cancelative Commutative Monoids
status_evidence.snippet: Studies asymptotic ω-primality but does not characterize numerical semigroups with ω(S) ≠ t(S).
status_evidence.claim: Recent (2023) work focuses on asymptotic invariants, not on the characterization problem.
